request: Select a facility, move the ghost to an arbitrary position and place it in the actual running game; track stalls and high function-call volume.
prior_coverage_gap: The prior matrix primarily selected catalogue entries by emitted signals, set exact numeric coordinates, and bound a rear-only Base fixture. Its final field click did not cover sustained pointer movement or the default connected world continuing beyond early observation windows. That coverage did not establish this player workflow was performant.

user_report.symptom: Almost freezes after moving and placing; reported hundreds of thousands of function calls versus about 30,000 before.
user_report.attachment_scope: Local pasted output, not assumed present in a fresh checkout. Available complete printed inspect_entity buckets do not establish hundreds of thousands per second; output overflow can truncate evidence.

implementation.world: Main creates its actual empty-field connected session. No Base replacement, explicit fast-forward, command stubs, scene-tree pause, cadence change, hidden performance whitelist or production gameplay modification.
implementation.speed: Build navigation and 1x are activated through GUI clicks; physics stays live until a detected issue pauses the test world.
inputs: Facility selection through an opened PopupMenu and keyboard navigation
Fractional arbitrary world points: workshop (83.375,48.625), depot (158.125,127.375)
Continuous pointer motion before and after placement
Wheel zoom, middle-button pan, R rotation and transformed pointer placement
Overlapping click rejection followed by motion and legal placement without restarting
Eight unaccumulated viewport motion events per rendered frame as an explicitly artificial stress case
At least twelve seconds planned for the no-building comparison; the normal run stops when its budget fails.
implementation.failure_behavior: Normal limits remain 100 ms frame/action and 30,000 full inspections per second. The probe pauses, saves current/complete failure records, counts, unique caller chains, engine errors and screenshots under logs/, and keeps subsequent phases pending. -ContinueAfterIssues runs the next isolated case; it does not certify the failed case.
implementation.measurement_limits: Engine GUI propagation is exercised, including transforms and popups; this is not physical OS polling. Counters cover instrumented entries only. Frame wall intervals include scheduling, rendering and logging; stack counts are not CPU shares. These four cases do not test every facility/state or replace the broader matrix.

verdict.normal_final_run: Four aggregate cases executed; three failed solely on frame-time budgets. No functional-contract or engine errors were recorded. One passing short stress case ends before the later default-world stall, so it is not evidence of long-run safety.

observed_normal_failures.label: Default game / click and observe workshop at 1x
Default game / overlap rejection then move and place without restarting
Default game / no selection or placement control at 1x

verdict.diagnostic_run: Explicitly raised frame/action stops to 1000 ms only to finish the sequence with traces. All four cases completed functional checks; this is not a normal-budget performance pass. The normal final run was executed afterward with unchanged defaults.
verdict.causal_inference: The no-selection/no-placement control also stalls around the same early simulation boundary. Pointer dispatch itself stayed below one millisecond in this trace, while frame gaps reached hundreds of milliseconds. The evidence points to shared default-world progression rather than an exclusively ghost-preview cause; it does not prove a single CPU culprit.
verdict.not_measured: Hundreds of thousands of inspect_entity entries per real second were not reproduced. Large cumulative instrumented totals and existing slower frame intervals are reproduced; the user may have a different world state or observation interval.

chain: IdentityLedger.move_entity emits person_position_changed for each moved person
Combat._on_person_position_changed scans squad rosters and invokes formation_changed
squad_cohesion calls Organization._active_roster_members, which exports each roster person
squad_cohesion exports each active person again to calculate positions/boarding
source_observed_amplification.interpretation: A moving squad repeats whole-squad detailed reads for each moved member. Complete-window caller counts corroborate this repeated export path in both placement and no-building controls. This is source/entry-count evidence, not exclusive CPU attribution; immediate cohort cohesion semantics must be preserved by any later fix.
